recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not change the current build severity or Provenance source under FHIR-3850; any future change from informational diagnostics to warnings or failures should be handled as a new tooling policy decision.
issue_request: FHIR-3850 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core change request reporting that Provenance.reason was CodeableConcept without a binding and that the build did not fail for that condition.
initial_application: Jira comments say the build began generating warnings. Git history confirms commit 465b04a3a62118caa464d86396fce67add7a69e4 added a ResourceValidator diagnostic for unbound CodeableConcept/Coding elements, and commit 6c026c5064671ebbd76e4679a2e250ea2074e89d added the ProvenanceReason binding to Provenance.reason with v3-PurposeOfUse.
additional_context: Current source no longer has Provenance.reason as the coded element. source/fhir.ini maps old Provenance.reason to active Provenance.authorization; current Provenance.authorization is CodeableConcept with an example ProvenanceReason binding, while Provenance.why carries free text as markdown. Later history deliberately reduced missing CodeableConcept/Coding binding diagnostics from warning to information, and suppressed-messages.txt shows the current build still emits that diagnostic class.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined branch and made no source edits.
